items.example: ex: It doesn't have to be a big present - it's just a token.

items.vn: (adverb). With the capacity to develop
items.example: ex: This crisis is potentially the most serious in the organization's history.

items.vn: (adjective). Full of the possibility of danger
items.example: ex: Teenagers often engage in risky behaviour.

items.vn: (verb). Catch fire or cause to catch fire.
items.example: ex: The fuel spontaneously ignites because of the high temperature and pressure.

items.vn: (verb). to burn the surface of something suddenly
items.example: ex: The heat from the explosion seared their hands and faces.

items.vn: (noun). the subject of a talk, a piece of writing, a person's thoughts, or an exhibition; a topic
items.example: ex: the theme of the sermon was reverence

items.vn: (verb). (of a sound) be repeated or reverberate after the original sound has stopped
items.example: ex: their footsteps echoed on the metal catwalks

items.vn: (verb). Use (something specified) as the foundation or starting point
items.example: ex: They took the decision to base their headquarters in Germany.

items.vn: (verb). Fit in with the wishes or needs of.
items.example: ex: The new policies fail to accommodate the disabled.

items.vn: (noun). a storage chamber for either liquid or gas
items.example: ex: We'll have to get a plumber in to look at that water tank.

items.vn: (noun). A yellow alloy of copper and zinc
items.example: ex: The door handles were made of brass.

items.vn: (noun). A device for controlling the passage of fluid or air through a pipe, duct, etc.,
items.example: ex: The valve failed to open/close.

items.vn: (verb). to press something firmly, especially with your fingers
items.example: ex: Cut the lemon in half and squeeze the juice into the bowl.

items.vn: (adjective). having artificially raised pressure.
items.example: ex: Aircraft cabins are pressurized.

items.vn: (verb). Go up or climb
items.example: ex: They slowly ascended the steep path up the mountain.

items.vn: (verb). Make partial or minor changes to (something)
items.example: ex: The proposals were unpopular and were only accepted in a modified form.

items.vn: (noun). the part by which a thing is held, carried, or controlled.
items.example: ex: I can't pick the kettle up - the handle's too hot.

items.vn: (noun). mineral oil that is found under the ground or the sea and is used to produce petrol/gas, paraffin, diesel oil, etc.
items.example: ex: Petrol and diesel are produced from petroleum.

items.vn: (noun). the part of a cooker, light, etc. that produces flame or heat
items.example: ex: Heat and light were provided by paraffin burners.

items.vn: (verb). Take on or assume (an attitude or position)
items.example: ex: They have no children of their own, but they're hoping to adopt.

items.vn: (verb). act as host at (an event) or for (a television or radio program).
items.example: ex: We thanked our hosts for a very enjoyable evening.

items.vn: (noun). A large metal pot with a lid and handle, used for cooking over an open fire.
items.example: ex: Nothing in the mash of rags can claim to be in its particular cauldron

items.vn: (noun). a type of table used in ceremonies in a Christian church or in other religious buildings
items.example: ex: Her gaze went to the altar, and she shivered

items.vn: (noun). A religious or solemn ceremony consisting of a series of actions
items.example: ex: Coffee and the newspaper are part of my morning ritual.

items.vn: (verb). to give your time or effort completely to something you believe in or to a person, or to use a particular amount of time or energy doing something
items.example: ex: He devoted his life to serving his family, friends, and neighbors.

items.vn: (adjective). disassociated from any specific instance
items.example: ex: Truth and beauty are abstract concepts.

items.vn: (noun). a piece of text, a formal suggestion, or a drawing in its original state, often containing the main ideas and intentions but not the developed form
items.example: ex: This is only a rough draft - the finished article will have pictures too.

items.vn: (adjective). Firm and stable in shape; not liquid or fluid.
items.example: ex: a white rose on a solid blue background

items.vn: (noun). An explosive
items.example: ex: "So you want to smell gunpowder?" he said to Pierre

items.vn: (noun). A small oval fruit
items.example: ex: Grapes and olives are superabundant in this part of France.

items.vn: (adjective). easily set on fire.
items.example: ex: We dont encourage the use of highly flammable materials

items.vn: (adjective). risky and dangerous
items.example: ex: We work in hazardous conditions

items.vn: (adjective). outside of sth
items.example: ex: In some of the villages the exterior walls of the houses are painted pink.

items.vn: (adjective). Likely to give way; not stable.
items.example: ex: That chair looks unstable to me.

items.vn: (adjective). connected with the inside of something
items.example: ex: He sustained injuries to his arms, legs, and several internal organs.

items.vn: (adjective). done as an experiment or test before introducing something more widely.
items.example: ex: If the pilot scheme is successful, many more homes will be offered the new television service.

items.vn: (verb). increase something.
items.example: ex: they finally agreed to bump up her salary

sections.title: Passage 1: Education Philosophy
sections.html:
statistics

(noun). the practice or science of collecting and analysing numerical data in large quantities

ex: The statistics show that, in general, women live longer than men.

mortality

(noun). The state of being subject to death.

ex: Her death made him more aware of his own mortality.

industrial

(adjective). Relating to or characterized by industry.

ex: He has an industrial background (= he has worked in industry).

premature

(adjective). happening before the normal or expected time

ex: Their criticisms seem premature considering that the results aren't yet known.

bury

(verb). Put or hide underground.

ex: His father is buried in the cemetery on the hill.

invest

(verb). provide or endow someone or something with (a particular quality or attribute)

ex: The institute will invest five million in the project.

newborn

(adjective). recently or just born

ex: Newborn infants, who have little immunity, are especially vulnerable to whooping cough.

consequence

(noun). A result or effect, commonly unpleasant

ex: I told the hairdresser to do what she wanted to my hair, and look at the consequences!

emotional

(adjective). connected with people’s feelings

ex: My doctor said the problem was more emotional than physical.

commitment

(noun). The state or quality of being dedicated to a cause, activity, etc.

ex: Players must make a commitment to play for a full season

infant

(noun). A very young child or baby.

ex: They're healthy infants

gutter

(noun). shallow trough fixed beneath the edge of a roof for carrying off rainwater.

ex: the line of intersection forms a descending gutter which runs to the outlet.

reference

(noun). The action of mentioning or alluding to something.

ex: I am writing with/in reference to (= in connection with) your letter of 15 March

pickle

(noun). A difficult situation

ex: Have some pickles with your sandwich.

modem

(noun). a device that connects one computer system to another using a telephone line so that data can be sent

ex: Televison and Internet are provided by high-speed modem.

educational

(adjective). relating to the provision of education.

ex: Reducing the size of classes may improve educational standards.

philosophy

(noun). A theory or attitude that acts as a guiding principle for behavior

ex: René Descartes is regarded as the founder of modern philosophy.

undergo

(verb). Experience or be subjected to something unpleasant

ex: She underwent an operation on a tumour in her left lung last year.

rural

(adjective). belong to the countryside

ex: The area is still very rural and undeveloped.

urban

(adjective). In, relating to, or characteristic of a town or city.

ex: Pollution has reached disturbingly high levels in some urban areas.

labour

(noun). work, especially hard physical work.

ex: The car parts themselves are not expensive, it's the labour that costs the money.

bulk

(noun). the mass or size of something large

ex: It was a document of surprising bulk.

manual

(adjective). involving using the hands or physical strength

ex: She tried to cure the pain in my knee by putting manual pressure on the joint.

technological

(adjective). connected with technology

ex: We'll see a tremendous lot of technological changes during/in our lifetime.

synonymous

(adjective). having the same, or nearly the same, meaning

ex: The words "annoyed" and "irritated" are more or less synonymous.

purchase

(verb). to buy something

ex: you must purchase your ticket 21 days in advance.

revolution

(noun). a change in the way a country is governed, usually to a different political system and often using violence or war (cuộc cách mạng)

ex: The country seems to be heading towards revolution.

exponentially

(adverb). more and more rapidly.

ex: We are growing exponentially in resources, people, and financing.

civil war

(noun). a war between citizens of the same country.

ex: The Spanish Civil War lasted from 1936 to 1939

influential

(adjective). Having great influence on someone or something.

ex: She wanted to work for a bigger and more influential (= powerful) newspaper.

comprehensive

(adjective). including all, or almost all details that may be concerned

ex: Is this list comprehensive or are there some names missing?

via

(preposition). through a place

ex: "I'll be back a little late because I'm going via town." "Uh-huh."

theory

(noun). a formal set of ideas that is intended to explain why something happens or exists

ex: He has a theory that the hole was caused by a meteorite.

colonial

(adjective). Relating to or characteristic of a colony or colonies

ex: Various parts of Africa have suffered under colonial rule.

recognition

(noun). identification of someone or something or person from previous encounters or knowledge

ex: There was no recognition of having done anything wrong.

inheritance

(noun). the money, property, etc. that you receive from somebody when they die; the fact of receiving something when somebody dies

ex: At 21 she came into her inheritance (= it was given to her).

concept

(noun). An abstract idea

ex: The concept of free speech is unknown to them.

noble

(adjective). Belonging by rank, title, or birth to the aristocracy

ex: His followers believe they are fighting for a noble cause.

savage

(adjective). fierce, violent, and uncontrolled

ex: That was a brutal and savage attack

uncorrupted

(adjective). Not corrupted

ex: Lucinda is uncorrupted by nefarious influences

novel

(noun). A fictitious prose narrative of book length, typically representing character and action

ex: Have you read any of Jane Austen's novels?

infancy

(noun). The state or period of babyhood or early childhood.

ex: Her youngest child died in infancy.

adulthood

(noun). the state of being an adult

ex: Responsibility, I suppose, is what defines adulthood.

extensive

(adjective). Covering or affecting a large area.

ex: Her knowledge of music is extensive (= she knows a lot about music).

adolescent

(noun). the process of developing from a child into an adult

ex: I'm looking after six adolescents for a week.

individuality

(noun). difference

ex: It's a competent essay but it lacks individuality.

developmental

(adjective). in a state of developing or being developed

ex: These diseases can lead to developmental delay in babies.

contrast

(noun). The state of being strikingly different from something else

ex: I like the contrast of the white trousers with the black jacket.

specific

(adjective). clearly defined or identified

ex: The virus attacks specific cells in the brain.

characteristic

(noun). A feature or quality belonging typically to a person, place, or thing

ex: Unfortunately a big nose is a family characteristic.

historical

(adjective). Of or concerning history or past events.

ex: She specializes in historical novels set in 18th-century England.

perspective

(noun). A particular attitude towards something; a point of view

ex: Her attitude lends a fresh perspective to the subject.

nurture

(verb). Care for and protect (someone or something) while they are growing.

ex: She wants to stay at home and nurture her children.

homelike

(adjective). belong to home

ex: "It doesn't look very homelike," said Dorothy, gazing around at the bare room.

application

(noun). A formal request to be considered for a position or to be allowed to do or have something

ex: Free information will be sent out on application to (= if you ask) the central office.

document

(verb). Record (something) in written, photographic, or other form.

ex: They are charged with using forged documents.

feral

(adjective). in a wild state, especially after escape from captivity or domestication.

ex: It's a feral cat

capture

(verb). Take into one's possession or control by force.

ex: Two of the soldiers were killed and the rest were captured.

Prepubescent

(adjective). relating to or in the period preceding puberty

ex: She's a prepubescent girl

forage

(verb). search widely for food or provisions

ex: gulls are equipped by nature to forage for food

profound

(adjective). very great; felt or experienced very strongly

ex: His mother's death when he was aged six had a very profound effect on him.

quash

(verb). Reject as invalid, especially by legal procedure

ex: The revolt was swiftly quashed by government troops.

optimistic

(adjective). Hopeful and confident about the future.

ex: She is optimistic about her chances of winning a gold medal.

physician

(noun). A person qualified to practice medicine.

ex: She is our family physician

civilise

(verb). To educate and improve a person or a society; to make somebody’s behaviour or manners better

ex: The Romans set out to civilize the Ancient Britons.

initiate

(verb). Cause (a process or action) to begin.

ex: Who initiated the violence?

subsidy

(noun). A sum of granted money

ex: The company received a substantial government subsidy.

recruit

(verb). find new people to join a company, an organization

ex: Having slimmed to around 1,400 staff, the company is now recruiting again.

semblance

(noun). The outward appearance or apparent form of something, especially when the reality is different.

ex: He was executed without even the semblance of a fair trial.

transformation

(noun). a complete change in somebody/something

ex: I'd never seen Jose in a tuxedo before - it was quite a transformation.

agrarian

(adjective). connected with farming and the use of land for farming

ex: This is prime agrarian land.

ruthless

(adjective). Having or showing no pity or compassion for others.

ex: Some people believe that to succeed in this world you have to be ruthless.

poverty

(noun). The state of being extremely poor.

ex: Two million people in the city live in abject (= very great) poverty.

substandard

(adjective). Below the usual or required standard

ex: There’s plenty of substandard child care available.

employment

(noun). the state of being employed

ex: How long have you been looking for employment?

painfully

(adverb). extremely, and in a way that makes you feel annoyed, upset, etc.

ex: I am painfully aware that I have made mistakes.

advance

(noun). a development or improvement.

ex: Recent advances in medical science mean that this illness can now be cured.

redefinition

(noun). the action or process of defining something again or differently.

ex: After the political changes of 1981, when a left-wing goverment came to power, the redefinition went on.

emergence

(noun). the fact of somebody/something coming out from a dark, confined or hidden place

ex: The agreement set the stage for the company's emergence from bankruptcy.

kindergarten

(noun). an establishment where children below the age of compulsory education play and learn

ex: Callie will start kindergarten in September.

movement

(noun). An act of moving.

ex: He made a sudden movement and frightened the bird away.

educator

(noun). a person who provides instruction or education; a teacher.

ex: Every society needs scientists, educators, and writers

notion

(noun). A belief about something

ex: I have only a vague notion of what she does for a living.

flourish

(adjective). grow or develop in a healthy or vigorous way

ex: Watercolour painting began to flourish in Britain around 1750.

basic

(noun). the essential facts or principles of a subject or skill.

ex: I'm learning the basics of the business

record

(noun). A thing constituting a piece of evidence about the past

ex: All medical records are kept confidential.

setting

(noun). the place or type of surroundings where something is positioned or where an event takes place

ex: Their house is in an idyllic country setting.

corruption

(noun). bad behaviour of people in authority

ex: Political corruption is widespread throughout the country.

prostitution

(noun). The practice or occupation of engaging in sexual activity with someone for payment.

ex: Poverty drove her to prostitution.

wealthy

(adjective). Having a great deal of money, resources, or assets; rich.

ex: He's a very wealthy man.

staple

(noun). a main product or part of something

ex: Phosphate has been a staple of this area for many years.

underdeveloped

(adjective). Not fully developed.

ex: It's in the poorer, underdeveloped eastern region of the country that the biggest problems exist.

drastic

(adjective). likely to have a strong or far-reaching effect

ex: Many employees have had to take drastic cuts in pay.

cornerstone

(noun). an important quality or feature on which a particular thing depends or is based

ex: In most countries, the family unit is still the cornerstone of society.

sections.title: Passage 2: How deserts are formed?
sections.html:
reference

(noun). The action of mentioning or alluding to something.

ex: She made a veiled reference to her former employer.

irregular

(adjective). Not even or balanced in shape or arrangement.

ex: Releasing the goods without an invoice is most irregular.

movement

(noun). An act of moving.

ex: He made a sudden movement and frightened the bird away.

particle

(noun). a very small piece of something

ex: Electrons are atomic particles.

vibrate

(verb). to move or make something move from side to side very quickly and with small movements

ex: His voice vibrated with anger.

jerk

(verb). make a sudden short sharp movement move

ex: "What's wrong?" she asked, jerking her head up.

initiate

(verb). khởi xướng - Cause (a process or action) to begin.

ex: Who initiated the violence?

chain reaction

(noun). a chemical reaction or other process in which the products themselves promote or spread the reaction

ex: The war risked setting off a perilous chain reaction that would endanger the whole world.

productive

(adjective). Achieving a significant amount or result

ex: He had an amazingly productive five years in which he managed to write four novels.

desert

(noun). A place with sand, hot weather and no vegetation

ex: They were lost in the desert for nine days.

farmland

(noun). land that is used for farming

ex: In the past 18 years, the average price of Iowa farmland has increased 234 percent.

barren

(adjective). not good enough for plants to grow on it

ex: We drove through a barren, rocky landscape.

arid

(adjective). too dry

ex: The desert is so arid that nothing can grow there.

technical

(adjective). connected with the practical use of machinery, methods, etc. in science and industry

ex: Personally, I found some parts of the book a little too technical to follow.

tackle

(verb). Make determined efforts to deal with an issue

ex: There are many ways of tackling this problem.

desertification

(noun). The process fertile land becomes desert

ex: Trees help to prevent desertification, as well as providing shade and firewood.

Satellite

(noun). An artificial body placed in orbit round the earth or moon or another planet

ex: The World Cup was transmitted around the world by satellite.

utilize

(verb). Make practical and effective use of.

ex: The vitamins come in a form that is easily utilized by the body.

investigate

(verb). Carry out research or study into a problem

ex: Police are investigating allegations of corruption involving senior executives.

livestock

(noun). Farm animals regarded as an asset

ex: The organic livestock industry has grown substantially in the last few years.

influence

(verb). have an influence on

ex: She's very good at making friends and influencing people.

migration

(noun). the movement of large numbers of people, birds or animals from one place to another

ex: Some old roads follow the paths of seasonal animal migrations.

invade

(verb). enter (a country or region) so as to subjugate or occupy it

ex: it was all part of a grander French plan to invade Ireland

refugee

(noun). A person who has been forced to leave their country in order to escape war, persecution, or natural disaster.

ex: Thousands of refugees fled across the border.

vulnerable

(adjective). Exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally

ex: I felt very vulnerable, standing there without any clothes on.

ecosystem

(noun). a biological community of interacting organisms and their physical environment

ex: Pollution can have disastrous effects on the delicately balanced ecosystem.

cultivation

(noun). the preparation and use of land for growing plants or crops

ex: The cultivation of wheat required the most fertile lands.

settlement

(noun). The process of establishing a settlement or settlements.

ex: A large Roman settlement has been discovered just outside the French town.

nomad

(noun). a member of a community that moves with its animals from place to place

ex: There's a tribe of Somalian desert nomads

graze

(verb). ăn cỏ

ex: The cows were grazing.

flock

(noun). a number of birds of one kind feeding, resting, or traveling together

ex: The shepherd is bringing his flock down from the hills.

herd

(noun). a group of animals of the same type that live and feed together

ex: Poor Janine - she just follows the herd

pasture

(noun). Land covered with grass and other low plants

ex: The sheep were grazing on the lush green pastures.

oasis

(noun). A fertile spot in a desert, where water is found.

ex: country of oases and burning desert sands

academic

(noun). A teacher or scholar in a university or other institute of higher education.

ex: The research company was founded by a group of academics from Stockholm University.

fatal

(adjective). causing death.

ex: This illness is fatal in almost all cases.

practice

(noun). The actual application or use of an idea, belief, or method

ex: How do you intend to put these proposals into practice, Mohamed?

crop

(noun). a cultivated plant grew to be eaten as grain, fruit or vegetable

ex: The main crops grown for export are coffee and rice.

progressively

(adverb). In a forward-looking, innovative manner.

ex: symptoms become progressively worse over a period of years

dry

(adjective). Free from moisture or liquid; not wet or moist.

ex: These plants grow well in dry soil/a dry climate.

region

(noun). part of a country or the world having definable characteristics

ex: There's a shortage of cheap housing in the region

drought

(noun). A prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall

ex: This year (a) severe drought has ruined the crops.

vegetation

(noun). Plants considered collectively

ex: The railway track will have to be cleared of vegetation if it is to be used again.

tract

(noun). an area of land, especially a large one

ex: There're large tracts of natural forest

devoid

(adjective). entirely lacking or free from

ex: Lisa kept her voice devoid of emotion

susceptible

(adjective). easily influenced by feelings and emotions

ex: These plants are particularly susceptible to frost.

erosion

(noun). The process of eroding or being eroded by wind, water, or other natural agents.

ex: soil erosion in this region is happening

ascertain

(verb). Find (something) out for certain; make sure of.

ex: Have you ascertained whether she's coming or not?

clear-cut

(adjective). easy to perceive or understand

ex: we now had a clear-cut objective

border

(noun). A line separating two countries, administrative divisions, or other areas.

ex: It's the northern border of their distribution area

landscape

(noun). everything you can see when you look across a large area of land

ex: the event transformed the political landscape

feature

(noun). a distinctive attribute or aspect of something.

ex: Our latest model of phone has several new features.

tremendous

(adjective). Very great in amount, scale, or intensity.

ex: They were making a tremendous amount of noise last night

publicity

(noun). the attention that is given to somebody/something by newspapers, television, etc.

ex: We have planned an exciting publicity campaign with our advertisers.

severe

(adjective). (of something bad or undesirable) very great; intense.

ex: There's a severe shortage of technicians

rainfall

(noun). the fall of rain.

ex: The average annual rainfall in this region is 750 mm.

misunderstanding

(noun). A failure to understand something correctly.

ex: There must be some misunderstanding. I never asked for these chairs to be delivered.

shortage

(noun). A state or situation in which something needed cannot be obtained i

ex: There's a shortage of food and shelter in the refugee camps.

precipitation

(noun). rain, snow, etc. that falls; the amount of this that falls

ex: Hail and sleet are types of precipitation.

farm

(verb). make one's living by growing crops or keeping livestock

ex: he has farmed organically for five years

soil

(noun). the upper layer of the earth in which plants grow

ex: Gardening is a way for city dwellers to return to the soil.

accelerate

(verb). Increase in rate, amount, or extent >< decelerate, stop, delay

ex: They use special chemicals to accelerate the growth of crops.

firewood

(noun). Wood burned as fuel

ex: We can use those old shelves as firewood.

chief

(adjective). most important

ex: The weather was our chief reason for coming here.

fuel

(noun). Material such as coal, gas, or oil that is burned to produce heat or power

ex: Wood, coal, oil, petrol, and gas are all different kinds of fuel.

planet

(noun). A celestial body moving

ex: Might there be intelligent life on other planets?

humidity

(noun). conditions in which the air is very warm and damp

ex: I don't like the humidity of this climate.

dust

(noun). a fine powder that consists of very small pieces of sand, earth, etc.

ex: The furniture was covered in dust and cobwebs.

phenomenon

(noun). A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen,

ex: Gravity is a natural phenomenon.

steady

(adjective). Firmly fixed

ex: The procession moved through the streets at a steady pace.

explosion

(noun). A violent blowing apart of something caused by a bomb

ex: The fire was thought to have been caused by a gas explosion.

impoverished

(adjective). (of a person or area) made poor.

ex: He is an impoverished young actor

destructive

(adjective). causing great and irreparable harm or damage

ex: Lack of trust is very destructive in a relationship.

thunderstorm

(noun). a storm with thunder and lightning and usually very heavy rain

ex: The rising of the sun, a thunderstorm, an earthquake are natural "phenomena."

topsoil

(noun). The top layer of soil.

ex: Use a combination of topsoil, sand and compost to create a well-draining soil for your herbs or get an organic potting mix

enforce

(verb). Compel observance of or compliance with a law

ex: The new teacher had failed to enforce any sort of discipline.

prospect

(noun). The possibility or likelihood of some future event occurring.

ex: Is there any prospect of the weather improving?

dryland

(noun). land as opposed to the sea or another body of water.

ex: the tide came in and cut off his route to dry land

alleviate

(verb). Make (suffering, deficiency, or a problem) less severe.

ex: he couldn't prevent her pain, only alleviate it

greenhouse

(noun). a glass building protecting plants from cold weather

ex: Gladys grows a lot of tomatoes in her greenhouse.

agriculture

(noun). The science or practice of farming, including cultivation of the soil

ex: The area depends on agriculture for most of its income.

compound

(noun). a thing that is composed of two or more separate elements; a mixture

ex: Salt is a compound of sodium and chlorine.

microalgae

(noun). microscopic algae, typically found in freshwater and marine systems, living in both the water column and sediment

ex: Nearly all research in algal biofuels has focused on culturing single species, or monocultures, of microalgae

livelihood

(noun). A means of securing the necessities of life.

ex: Their rule was that they had to earn their livelihood, and must not beg

sections.title: Passage 3: The Olympic Torch
sections.html:
torch

(noun). a small light that is held in the hand and usually gets its power from batteries

ex: Kris lit another torch to display a darkened case on the wall.

Committee

(noun). a group of people appointed for a specific function, typically consisting of members of a larger group

ex: She sits on/is on the school's development committee.

withstand

(verb). to be strong enough not to be damaged

ex: Our toys are designed to withstand the rough treatment of the average five-year-old.

severe

(adjective). (of something bad or undesirable) very great; intense.

ex: This is a school for children with severe learning difficulties.

aesthetic

(adjective). appreciation with beauty

ex: The new building has little aesthetic value/appeal.

practical

(adjective). connected with real situations rather than with ideas or theories

ex: Qualifications are important but practical experience is always a plus.

value

(verb). estimate the monetary worth of (something)

ex: He valued the painting at $2,000.

purchase

(verb). to buy something

ex: Tickets must be purchased two weeks in advance.

relay

(noun). a group of people or animals engaged in a task or activity for a fixed period of time and then replaced by a similar group

ex: Relays of workers kept the machines going through the night.

treasurable

(adjective). Highly valued; prized

ex: Recent Examples on the Web Many of the performances are nonpareil, attesting to the treasurable artistry of the one and only Slava

souvenir

(noun). a thing that you buy and/or keep to remind yourself of a place, an occasion or a holiday/vacation

ex: We brought back a few souvenirs from our holiday in Mexico.

liquid

(noun). a substance that flows freely and is not a solid or a gas, for example water or oil

ex: Mercury is a liquid at room temperature.

promote

(verb). Support or actively encourage (a cause, venture, etc.); further the progress of

ex: It has long been known that regular exercise promotes all-round good health

security

(noun). the state of being free from danger or threat.

ex: The station was closed for two hours because of a security alert.

appearance

(noun). an act of becoming visible or noticeable; an arrival.

ex: the sudden appearance of her daughter startled her

environmentally

(adverb). in a way that relates to the natural world and the impact of human activity on its condition

ex: industries that work in an environmentally responsible way

substance

(noun). A particular kind of matter with uniform properties.

ex: What sort of substance could withstand those temperatures?

flame

(noun). a hot bright stream of burning gas that comes from something that is on fire

ex: The flames grew larger as the fire spread.

bright

(adjective). giving out or reflecting much light; shining.

ex: The rooms were bright and airy.

detrimental

(adjective). harmful

ex: Their decision could be detrimental to the future of the company.

slender

(adjective). (of people or their bodies) thin in an attractive or elegant way

ex: He put his hands around her slender waist.

steel

(noun). a hard, strong, gray or bluish-gray alloy of iron with carbon and usually other elements, used extensively as a structural and fabricating material

ex: Those are steel girders

rod

(noun). long straight piece of wood, metal or glass

ex: He was given a fishing rod for his birthday.

circular

(adjective). Having the form of a circle.

ex: the building features a circular atrium

platform

(noun). A raised level surface on which people or things can stand.

ex: He stepped up onto the platform and looked out into the audience

jet

(verb). Spurt out in jets

ex: Blood jetted from his nostrils

inscribe

(verb). marked with characters.

ex: The prize winners each receive a book with their names inscribed on the first page.

token

(noun). something that is a symbol of a feeling, a fact, an event, etc.

ex: It doesn't have to be a big present - it's just a token.

potentially

(adverb). With the capacity to develop

ex: This crisis is potentially the most serious in the organization's history.

risky

(adjective). Full of the possibility of danger

ex: Teenagers often engage in risky behaviour.

ignite

(verb). Catch fire or cause to catch fire.

ex: The fuel spontaneously ignites because of the high temperature and pressure.

sear

(verb). to burn the surface of something suddenly

ex: The heat from the explosion seared their hands and faces.

theme

(noun). the subject of a talk, a piece of writing, a person's thoughts, or an exhibition; a topic

ex: the theme of the sermon was reverence

echo

(verb). (of a sound) be repeated or reverberate after the original sound has stopped

ex: their footsteps echoed on the metal catwalks

base

(verb). Use (something specified) as the foundation or starting point

ex: They took the decision to base their headquarters in Germany.

accommodate

(verb). Fit in with the wishes or needs of.

ex: The new policies fail to accommodate the disabled.

tank

(noun). a storage chamber for either liquid or gas

ex: We'll have to get a plumber in to look at that water tank.

brass

(noun). A yellow alloy of copper and zinc

ex: The door handles were made of brass.

valve

(noun). A device for controlling the passage of fluid or air through a pipe, duct, etc.,

ex: The valve failed to open/close.

squeeze

(verb). to press something firmly, especially with your fingers

ex: Cut the lemon in half and squeeze the juice into the bowl.

pressurised

(adjective). having artificially raised pressure.

ex: Aircraft cabins are pressurized.

ascend

(verb). Go up or climb

ex: They slowly ascended the steep path up the mountain.

modify

(verb). Make partial or minor changes to (something)

ex: The proposals were unpopular and were only accepted in a modified form.

handle

(noun). the part by which a thing is held, carried, or controlled.

ex: I can't pick the kettle up - the handle's too hot.

petroleum

(noun). mineral oil that is found under the ground or the sea and is used to produce petrol/gas, paraffin, diesel oil, etc.

ex: Petrol and diesel are produced from petroleum.

burner

(noun). the part of a cooker, light, etc. that produces flame or heat

ex: Heat and light were provided by paraffin burners.

adopt

(verb). Take on or assume (an attitude or position)

ex: They have no children of their own, but they're hoping to adopt.

host

(verb). act as host at (an event) or for (a television or radio program).

ex: We thanked our hosts for a very enjoyable evening.

cauldron

(noun). A large metal pot with a lid and handle, used for cooking over an open fire.

ex: Nothing in the mash of rags can claim to be in its particular cauldron

altar

(noun). a type of table used in ceremonies in a Christian church or in other religious buildings

ex: Her gaze went to the altar, and she shivered

ritual

(noun). A religious or solemn ceremony consisting of a series of actions

ex: Coffee and the newspaper are part of my morning ritual.

devote

(verb). to give your time or effort completely to something you believe in or to a person, or to use a particular amount of time or energy doing something

ex: He devoted his life to serving his family, friends, and neighbors.

abstract

(adjective). disassociated from any specific instance

ex: Truth and beauty are abstract concepts.

draft

(noun). a piece of text, a formal suggestion, or a drawing in its original state, often containing the main ideas and intentions but not the developed form

ex: This is only a rough draft - the finished article will have pictures too.

solid

(adjective). Firm and stable in shape; not liquid or fluid.

ex: a white rose on a solid blue background

gunpowder

(noun). An explosive

ex: "So you want to smell gunpowder?" he said to Pierre

olive

(noun). A small oval fruit

ex: Grapes and olives are superabundant in this part of France.

flammable

(adjective). easily set on fire.

ex: We dont encourage the use of highly flammable materials

hazardous

(adjective). risky and dangerous

ex: We work in hazardous conditions

exterior

(adjective). outside of sth

ex: In some of the villages the exterior walls of the houses are painted pink.

unstable

(adjective). Likely to give way; not stable.

ex: That chair looks unstable to me.

internal

(adjective). connected with the inside of something

ex: He sustained injuries to his arms, legs, and several internal organs.

pilot

(adjective). done as an experiment or test before introducing something more widely.

ex: If the pilot scheme is successful, many more homes will be offered the new television service.

bump up

(verb). increase something.

ex: they finally agreed to bump up her salary
